statement.p: Find the area between y = 2 \sin x and y = 4 \cos x over the interval \left[0,\pi\right]. Sketch the curves if necessary.

static.solution:
Over the interval [0,\pi], the graphs y = 2\sin x and y = 4 \cos x intersect when 2\sin x = 4 \cos x, i.e., \tan x = \frac{4}{2}, i.e., x=\tan^{-1}(\frac{4}{2})=1.10714871779409.
Let t = \tan^{-1}(\frac{4}{2}).
Over the interval \left[0, t\right], the graph of y = 2\sin x lies below that of y = 4 \cos x. Hence, the area between the two curves is \int_0^{ t}(4 \cos x-2 \sin x)dx \begin{array}{ll} \amp =\left.(4\sin x+2\cos x)\right|_0^{ t} \cr \amp =\left(4\sin t+2\cos t\right)-(4\cdot 0+2\cdot 1)\cr \amp =\left(4\sin t+2\cos t\right)-2 \end{array}
Since t = \tan^{-1}(\frac{4}{2}), we have \tan t = \frac{4}{2}. Considering a rightangle triangle with an angle which opposite side has length 4 and adjacent side has length 2, we see that the hypotenues is \sqrt{20}. Thus \sin t = \frac{4}{\sqrt{20}} and \cos t = \frac{2}{\sqrt{20}}.
4\sin t+2\cos t = \frac{4^2}{\sqrt{20}} + \frac{2^2}{\sqrt{20}} = \frac{4^2+2^2}{\sqrt{20}} = \frac{20}{\sqrt{20}}=\sqrt{20}.
Thus, \int_0^{ t}(4 \cos x-2 \sin x)dx= \sqrt{20}-2.
Over the interval \left[ t,\pi\right], the graph of y = 2\sin x lies above that of y = 4 \cos x. Hence, the area between the two curves is \int^\pi_{ t}(2\sin x - 4 \cos x)dx \begin{array}{ll} \amp =-\left.(4\sin x+2\cos x)\right|^\pi_{ t} \cr \amp =2 + \sqrt{20} \end{array}
Thus the total area is the sum of the above two integrals, which is 2\sqrt{20}.
